best_for: People who want a free VPN with no data cap for public Wi-Fi, and who might pay later for streaming, more countries and more devices.

points.title: The free plan is real but narrow
points.text: Proton Free has no stated data cap, no ads and a no-logs policy. It allows one device at a time, connects to 10 countries picked at random, and runs at medium speed. Streaming and P2P are listed as paid features.

points.title: What VPN Plus costs
points.text: VPN Plus is USD 2.99 per month on a 12-month plan, billed USD 35.88 the first year and USD 83.88 a year after that. It covers 10 devices, 140+ countries and 20,000+ servers. Proton Unlimited, at USD 6.49 per month, adds Mail, Drive and Pass. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Paid extras on the desktop
points.text: On Windows, paid plans add Secure Core routing, the NetShield ad and malware blocker, split tunneling and VPN Accelerator. The kill switch and leak protection come with the free plan. Proton offers a 30-day money-back guarantee.

points.title: Linux: Proton's own repository
points.text: Proton supports its Linux app on the latest stable Debian and Ubuntu with GNOME, installed from its own repository or as a Snap. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that is not marked verified. If you uninstall, remove the kill switch connections by hand.

points.title: Three apps, three version numbers
points.text: Each system has its own app and version line: 5.1.10 on Windows, 6.5.2 on macOS and 4.18.8 on Linux. Do not compare numbers across systems.

points.title: Windows on Arm is native
points.text: Windows gets separate x64 and Arm64 installers that install for the whole machine. The Mac app is universal and needs macOS 14. The Windows listing keeps 32 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Open source
points.text: Proton says all its VPN apps are open source and audited, and the desktop apps are GPL-3.0.
